title: Dear Filolial-sama,
text: “Is there a Demi-Human who facilitated the intrusion?”

The next day, the people from Siltvelt reported this to us. The messenger explained the situation with an apologetic expression. It seems we have enemies beyond the Three Heroes Church. Upon hearing this, Éclair looked puzzled and spoke up.
“Weren’t we supposed to have strict security in place?”
“I mean, if they’re Demi-Humans, they’re supposed to be on our side, right? Why would they do something like that?”
“Well… it seems there’s a plot by those with ties to Shieldfreeden to prevent the Shield Hero from being welcomed into Siltvelt.”
“Hmm, it’s true that the Shield Hero is a rare figure among Demi-Humans. I was aware that his mere presence could spark conflict, but…”
“It’s almost as if the whole world is out to get me.”

My Father muttered quietly, hanging his head. Now that you mention it, it does seem that way. In Melromarc, he’s regarded as the god of an enemy nation; in Siltvelt and Shieldfreeden, there’s internal strife among the Demi-Humans. It’s not exactly a favorable situation.
“Don’t worry, Father. Even if the whole world becomes my enemy, I, Motoyasu, will destroy every single one of your enemies.”
“Huh? Oh, yeah. But destroying them all might be going a bit too far…”
“Lord Iwatani, this is a difficult diplomatic issue. Please don’t let it get you down.”
“Sakura will definitely protect Naofumi, right?”
“Thank you, Eclair, and Sakura-chan.”
Sakura-chan comforted her Father. How kind-hearted of her. I, Motoyasu, am so moved that tears are welling up in my eyes.
“From now on, the number of assassins from the Three Heroes Church will decrease, but can we assume assassins will come from Shieldfreeden next?”
“Shieldfreeden is supposed to be a country that publicly proclaims equality and freedom for Demi-Humans and humans, though…”

Éclair is scratching her head with a “crunch, crunch” sound, looking utterly exasperated. Shieldfreeden. If I recall correctly, that was the country that didn’t join my Father’s battle in the first world. …My memory’s a bit fuzzy around here—I can’t quite remember if they were allies or enemies. To begin with, I was so preoccupied with Filolial-sama that I left all those matters entirely up to my Father. All I can do is follow my Father’s orders to the letter.
“It seems every world has its share of similar diplomatic issues, doesn’t it?”
“My future Father would do whatever it takes to cause the other side trouble. Let’s head to Siltvelt.”
“Mr. Kitamura, I think there are more tactful ways to put that…”
“Well… I don’t intend to just sit here quietly and let myself be killed, and if they attack, I’ll have no choice but to fight back.”
My Father replied, seeming convinced. But…
“Actually, maybe it would’ve been better if I hadn’t been summoned?”

“The fault lies with the people of this world who are trying to eliminate Lord Iwatani solely for religious reasons while a wave of calamity is upon us. As a representative of this world, I apologize.”
Éclair bowed her head to Father. Hoho. That’s quite a noble attitude. Even though he’s a hero, he’s still human. He’s not a machine designed to save the world, but a being with a heart and soul.
And my Father, too, is a human being first and foremost, before he’s a hero. Furthermore, I am The Love Hunter. I’ll live according to my Father’s wishes.

Above all, someone as cold-hearted as a machine could never save the world. What’s needed is someone with a heart—someone kind, sincere, and true to their word. I, Motoyasu, haven’t reached that level yet, but I’ll do my best to fight for my Father, Filo-tan, and Filolial-sama.
“Ms. Eclair… Yeah, you’re right. It’s the hero’s duty to fight to save the world from the waves of destruction, isn’t it?”
“Ah, Lord Iwatani and Lord Kitamura were summoned to this world for that very purpose. It was a mistake to entangle religion in it… For now, let’s prioritize getting Lord Iwatani safely to Siltvelt.”
“Yeah. Well then, let’s get going.”
We had Yuki-chan and the others pull the carriage, and we resumed our journey.

The journey from there can best be described as going smoothly. Thanks to Father’s improved Defense Power, dealing with assassins became a breeze. Even when they attacked, we could easily scatter them.

Occasionally, large-scale Ceremonial Magic attacks would strike along the highways, but I nullified them with spells like “Liberation” and “Absorb,” counterattacked every one, immediately arrested the perpetrators, transported them to a nearby town, and continued on our way. Eventually, even the assassins came to realize the Hero’s strength and stopped coming out. There were no more reckless assaults.
“Kue”

I spotted some wild Filolial-samas. I leaned out of the carriage to gaze at them. Wild Filolial-samas… they possess a free-spirited nature and wild charm that domesticated Filolial-samas lack. Above all, wild Filolial-samas tend to cherish their herds. Their sense of unity possesses a heart-stirring beauty that cannot be expressed in a single word.
“Motoyasu-sama! Please look at us, not those creatures!”
“Ha ha ha! I cherish all Filolial-samas equally.”
“You really do love them, don’t you, Motoyasu-kun… Why don’t you treat Yuki-chan and the others a little more specially?”
“All Filolial-sama are equally special, you know.”
“No good. Lord Kitamura isn’t getting the message.”
Did I say something strange? I haven’t the faintest idea.
“Hmm…? Naofumi, what do you think of those kids?”
“What do you mean…? Just that there are Filolial-sama in the wild, too, I guess?”
“I see…”
Sakura-chan and her Father get along well, don’t they?
Oh? That reaction from those Filolials looks familiar. They ran off in a flurry. Or was that just my imagination?
“Ah… they’re gone.”
“That’s just how wild Filolials are. Sure, there are all kinds of species, but they aren’t that aggressive.”
“Is that so? Come to think of it, I heard that for them to take on a form like Yuki-chan and the others, a Hero has to raise them, right?”
“That’s right.”
“It’s true that their appearances are so different, and seeing them take human form is one surprise after another, but if it’s because a Hero raises them, that makes sense.”
“Didn’t Heroes in the past raise Filolials? You’d think there’d be something about that in the records.”
“Well, there are plenty of anecdotes about the number of heroes… Among those who raised monsters to be strong, the Hero of the Seven-Star Whip is particularly famous.”

Hmm…? I feel like I’m about to remember something unpleasant. Just the word “whip” makes me feel uncomfortable. …I feel like something sad happened, but I can’t quite remember what. Still, it’s better to be on guard.
“So maybe there are a lot of monsters that develop in special ways when raised by a hero.”
“Just the Filolials alone are causing this much commotion. I’ll pass on that.”
“Ahaha, it looks like Ms. Eclair has her hands full teaching Yuki-chan and the others proper etiquette, doesn’t it?”
“Why are you acting like this has nothing to do with you…? Lord Iwatani is swamped with meal preparations, isn’t he?”
“Hahaha… You’re right.”
What a peaceful atmosphere. It’s fun mingling with the conversation among the envoys from Siltvelt.
It happened the following night. As we were all camping, fireflies began fluttering around us. Then, from afar, we heard the voices of Filolial-sama and his companions calling out, “Gua-gua.”
“W-what is it?”
“What’s going on?”
“It sounds like they’re saying we should all head over here.”
That’s what Yuki-chan replied.
“What!? Are you saying there are assassins among the Filolials too?”
“No, that’s not it.”

Éclair and my Father grew more wary of the changes in the surroundings. At that moment, I remembered what was happening: the only Filolial—other than Filo-tan—who had ever caught my eye was about to arrive. The Filolials were gathering around us, making “gua-gua” sounds.
“Do you know, Lord Kitamura? What’s going to happen?”
“A big Filolial-sama is coming.”
“Huh? Please explain it in simpler terms.”
“The Filolial-sama who’s second only to Filo-tan in charm is coming.”
“This isn’t working… Lord Iwatani, I can’t have a proper conversation with Lord Kitamura.”
“Yeah, Sakura-chan. What are the Filolials around us saying?”
“Um… they were saying something about ‘let’s all go together’?”
“So, a big Filolial is coming? Is this the story of the Queen of the Filolials from legend?”
Éclair was looking around nervously.
“We’re not going to get attacked and eaten, are we?”
“Filolials are omnivores, after all. The painful part is that I can’t rule out that possibility.”

Before long, the Filolial-samas had completely surrounded us, staring at us from the darkness. In the light of the fireflies, I could see that there were various species of Filolial-samas among them. Ah… I’ve thought this many times before, but this really is a paradise for the Filolial-samas. Soon, a single Filolial-sama appeared, and I—…
